notes:
Summary: Scriptorium runs a historical film/audio archive plus associated metadata (press kits, transcripts, curator notes). Primary product need: low-latency, high-relevance search for editors and public-facing discovery UI. They want a two-stage RAG retrieval pipeline: dense vector retrieval for recall + a cross-encoder reranker for precision on top-K. Key constraints: long documents (avg 8k tokens), heavy cost sensitivity, and strict EU/NA residency for parts of dataset.

Indexing scale and chunking:
- Current estimate: 8M source items -> after semantic chunking and OCR cleanup ~30-40M chunks. POC will start with 500k sources (~2M chunks).
- Discussed chunking strategies: semantic paragraph split (NER/section headings) vs fixed-token sliding window. Tradeoffs noted: larger chunks reduce ANN lookup pressure but increase embedding token cost; sliding window (1k token window, 200 token overlap) gives better recall at title/quote boundaries.
- They prefer storing chunk start/end offsets and source mappings for HUD-level highlight + provenance.

Retrieval + reranking architecture discussion:
- Two-stage approach agreed: bi-encoder (dense) for top-500 retrieval, then cross-encoder rerank top-20. Need to validate K (candidate pool) vs latency/cost.
- Cross-encoder models (deeper Transformer) give best precision but add per-query token cost; team asked for recommendations to balance: smaller cross-encoder for interactive queries (<200ms target) and fallback to cheaper scoring for high-throughput analytics.
- Consider offline reranking/score augmentation for frequently asked queries (precompute rerank features) to reduce real-time compute.

Latency & cost targets:
- UX target: P95 < 300ms for editor search, P50 < 150ms. Production throughput target: 50 QPS for peak editorial workflows; occasional spikes to 150 QPS during ingest windows.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to keep incremental per-query cost (embedding + ANN + reranker) below $0.02 for typical editorial queries; willing to accept $0.10 for high-value research queries. Asking Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching & cache policies.

Indexing & ANN choices:
- Discussed HNSW memory footprint vs IVF+PQ disk-backed approach. Team leans toward hybrid: hot HNSW shards for recent/popular content + IVF+PQ for cold archive to control memory. Need Redwood guidance on shard sizing and autoscale behavior on Dedicated.

Evaluation & quality:
- They will supply a labeled relevance set (2k queries with graded relevance) to benchmark recall/precision and tune reranker threshold. Also want regression alerts on eval sets.
- SE proposed initial metric goals: MAP@20 >= 0.38 and NDCG@10 >= 0.62 for editorial workflows.

Security/compliance notes:
- Must run inside customer VPC or on-prem for EU-resident alt-media collections. KMS integration required for envelope encryption. SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Open technical questions / blockers:
- Precise estimate for Dedicated GPU count and memory given hybrid ANN + cross-encoder reranker.
- Legal needs a redline on content retention (30/90/365-day tiers) and deletion guarantees for public requests.
- Need cost model showing incremental $/query at 50 QPS and at 150 QPS for Dedicated vs Hosted.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Index 500k sources -> ~2M chunks within 7 days, measure ingest throughput and embedding time.
- 50 QPS load test with P95 < 350ms and average relevance improvement (NDCG@10) vs current baseline by +15%.
- Clear cost estimate per 1M queries and recommended Dedicated sizing.

Short quotes/paraphrases from calls: "Can we keep editor queries snappy — they won't tolerate 800ms waits"; "If reranker costs triple, we need intelligent fallback policies".

- Marcus to provision Dedicated trial cluster and run indexing pilot (week of 2024-11-25).
- Jordan to deliver cost delta sheet and recommended reranker model families.
- Legal + Security sync scheduled (2024-11-28).
